sentences: A linear sketch over F2 records selected parities of a Boolean input.
The question compares the minimum randomized sketch length for f with randomized one-way communication for computing \(f(x \mathrm{XOR} y)\).
Alice knows x and sends one message to Bob, who knows y and must determine the function value.
An exact deterministic correspondence is known in the source, and the conjecture asks for a randomized correspondence up to polylogarithmic factors.
A proof would show that arbitrary one-way messages offer little extra power over linear measurements for this broad class of XOR-based communication problems.
